newsitem.title: USA: New Britain, Conn., faces budget gap - paper.
newsitem.headline: New Britain, Conn., faces budget gap - paper.

text.p: New Britain, Conn., officials, faced with closing a $1.5 million budget gap, are considering layoffs and cuts in services, though the mayor proposed a bond offering, the Hartford Courant said Friday.

The paper quoted Susan McMullen, executive aide to Mayor Lucian Pawlak, as saying raising taxes was out of the question. Pawlak said he thought the answer was selling $114 million of municipal bonds to cover increasing payments for police and fire pensions.
But the paper said even some of the mayor's supporters thought his plan was too risky, and his opponents thus far have deprived him of the crucial vote to authorize the sale.

The year's pension payment of $924,660 accounts for most of the decifit, though there are other shortfalls in education, private school bus transportation and sewer funds, Pawlak said, before a Wednesday session of the council.
